comments.note: AC-3 / AC-5 BLOCKER — Missing /* START METHODS */ and /* END METHODS */ markers in HCP Editor target files. CustomIcon.php (at assets/classes/Maileditor/CustomIcon.php) and custom-icon.js (at themes/default/js/ui/custom-icon.js) on the feature-icon-builder branch do not contain the /* START METHODS */ / /* END METHODS */ markers required by IconBuilder. WP-010 was supposed to add markers to CustomIcon.php (before line 30 '// region: Icon type methods', and after line 185 '// endregion'), and WP-011 was supposed to add them to custom-icon.js (before '// region: Icon methods' at line 14, and after '// endregion' at line 55). Both WPs were marked COMPLETE but the changes were never committed — git log shows no commit adding these markers to either file. Fix: add the markers to both files and commit them to the HCP Editor feature-icon-builder branch.

Cosmetic path construction double-slash: In Maileditor/Composer/ComposerScripts.php, self::$rootFolder is a FolderInfo whose __toString() returns the path with a trailing slash (because FolderInfo::factory(__DIR__.'/../../../..') → normalizePath keeps the trailing /). Prepending '/' to path segments then produces double-slash paths like ...Composer/../../../..//assets/.... Unix resolves this correctly so there is no functional impact, but it creates confusing error messages. Fix: use self::$rootFolder . 'assets/...' (without leading slash) or use rtrim((string)self::$rootFolder, '/') consistently.

comments.note: BLOCKING — Framework WP-008 integration is absent. git status confirms src/classes/Application/Composer/ComposerScripts.php and composer.json have zero staged or committed changes relative to the feature-icon-builder branch HEAD (commit 86cb38c5). The rebuildIcons() and doRebuildIcons() methods do not exist in ComposerScripts.php (grep returns no results), and the 'rebuild-icons' script is not in composer.json (verified by parsing the scripts object). Required fix: (1) Add 'use Application\Composer\IconBuilder\IconBuilder;' import to ComposerScripts.php. (2) Add a public rebuildIcons() method that calls self::init() then self::doRebuildIcons(). (3) Add private doRebuildIcons() method that resolves the framework root via FolderInfo::factory(__DIR__.'/../../../../'), constructs paths to icons.json / Icon.php / icon.js, invokes IconBuilder::build(), and echoes progress messages. (4) Insert self::rebuildIcons() in build() between generateCSSClassesJS() and updateContextGenerateDate(). (5) Add 'rebuild-icons': 'Application\\Composer\\ComposerScripts::rebuildIcons' to composer.json scripts. Note: WP-008 was previously reviewed as PASS and the code-review pipeline documented a Reviewer-applied fix (realpath → FolderInfo::factory pattern). The same pattern must be used in the new implementation.

BLOCKING (consequence) — WP-014 AC-2 ('Running composer rebuild-icons twice in the framework results in zero git diff on the second run') cannot be validly verified because the rebuild-icons script does not exist in the framework's composer.json. The QA agent's PASS for this criterion appears to have been recorded without actually running the composer script. After the Developer applies the WP-008 integration, QA must re-verify AC-2 by executing 'composer rebuild-icons' in the framework root.

IconCollection::getByID() docblock: replaced the erroneous '{@see self::normaliseID()}' usage hint with the correct str_replace() example. normaliseID() is a private method — callers cannot invoke it. The fix removes the private-method reference and replaces it with 'str_replace(array(\'-\', \' \'), \'_\', $id)' and a note to use idExists() before calling getByID(). Non-behavioral — only the docblock was changed.

[documentation-forward] IconCollection::getByID() throws a bare \RuntimeException instead of the project's ApplicationException pattern. This is a conscious deviation for programmer-error scenarios, but the module-level documentation (and any generated CTX docs) should note this exception type, its message format, and the recommendation to call idExists() beforehand to avoid it.

All framework IconBuilder classes (IconBuilder, IconDefinition, IconsReader, AbstractLanguageRenderer, PHPRenderer, JSRenderer) and UI\Icons classes (IconCollection, IconInfo) are architecturally sound. Code quality, separation of concerns, docblocks, error codes, and test coverage are all clean. The HCP Editor ComposerScripts integration is correct and follows established patterns. No other blocking or fix-forward items found.
